subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: For spawned subagent runs that cannot use the selected Codex/OpenAI OAuth route, should OpenClaw fail closed, warn visibly before fallback, or allow the current fallback once main-auth inheritance is proven?
rationale: Source now supports inherited OAuth, but the issue also raises a security and billing-sensitive fallback policy that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require live proof and visible fallback policy
options.body: Run the current-main live subagent Codex OAuth probe and require an explicit warning or fail-closed behavior before closing any remaining fallback concern.

options.title: Close after source proof only
options.body: Treat the inherited main-auth implementation and regression tests as sufficient and track fallback visibility separately only if a new report reproduces it.

options.title: Keep fallback permissive
options.body: Accept silent provider fallback as intentional for availability once the selected OAuth profile is inherited correctly.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and visible fallback policy
recommendation.body: Run the current-main live subagent Codex OAuth probe and require an explicit warning or fail-closed behavior before closing any remaining fallback concern.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent current-main implementation and tests for inherited auth-profile ownership are attributed to this history.
